summary: The note describes exhibition games in North American professional sports, where teams played non-regular-season contests. It covers MLB interleague exhibitions such as the Pearson Cup and Mayor's Trophy Game, NBA preseason games against ABA teams, Harlem Globetrotters challenges, and NBA preseason games in Europe and Asia. It also notes that NBA teams now play eight preseason games, often at neutral sites, and mentions exhibition hockey teams such as the Flying Fathers and the Buffalo Sabres Alumni Hockey Team.
one_line: Overview of exhibition games in North American pro sports, including MLB, NBA and exhibition hockey matchups.
key_facts: Several MLB teams used to play regular exhibition games against nearby teams in the other major league, but regular-season interleague play made such games unnecessary.
The Toronto Blue Jays and Montreal Expos met annually in the Pearson Cup exhibition game.
The Pearson Cup tradition ended when the Expos moved to Washington DC for the 2005 season.
The New York Yankees played in the Mayor's Trophy Game against various local rivals from 1946 to 1983.
From 1971 to 1975, NBA teams played preseason exhibitions against American Basketball Association teams.
In the 2006 and 2007 seasons, the NBA and the Euroleague conducted a preseason tournament featuring two NBA teams and the finalists from that year's Euroleague.
In the 1998-99 and 2011-12 seasons, NBA teams were limited to only two preseason games due to lockouts.
National Basketball Association teams play eight preseason games per year.
Today NBA teams mainly play preseason games at neutral sites within their market areas so fans who cannot easily attend regular-season games can see a game close to home.
The Phoenix Suns schedule one exhibition game yearly at Indian Wells Tennis Garden in Indian Wells, California, the only instance of an NBA game in an outdoor venue.
The Flying Fathers, a Canadian group of Catholic priests, regularly toured North America playing exhibition hockey games for charity.
Les Costello, a onetime NHL player, was one of the Flying Fathers' founders and was ordained as a priest after retiring from professional hockey.
The Buffalo Sabres Alumni Hockey Team is composed almost entirely of retired NHL players, most of whom played at least part of their career for the Buffalo Sabres.
